title: AIPAC Lost BIG In The Midterms - and Zeteo’s New Documentary Goes Inside the Lobby’s Waning Influence.
author: Team Zeteo
content:
The 2026 midterms '[bluenami](https://zeteo.com/p/9-impressive-midterm-wins-
you-may)' was more than just a rousing defeat of Republicans and MAGA. It was
also a defeat of AIPAC, the powerful pro-Israel lobby. More than [two-thirds
of the $84m](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/7/how-did-aipac-backed-
candidates-fare-in-the-us-midterm-elections) it spent this cycle went to
candidates who lost, according to the Quincy Institute for Responsible
Statecraft. As [Politico](https://www.politico.com/newsletters/politico-
influence/2026/11/05/aipacs-dwindling-allies-in-
congress-01152410?template_id=OT5J0E7B7DD7&is_login_link=true) reports, more
than 30 AIPAC-backed candidates also lost, totalling three quarters of
competitive races.

Its biggest defeats were in Michigan and Maine, where Democrats Abdul El-Sayed
and Troy Jackson won their respective Senate Races.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

AIPAC's losses are now raising questions about whether its influence in U.S.
politics is waning, about its relationship with the Israeli government, and if
it is acting as a foreign agent. Zeteo explores all of that in a timely,
original documentary, '**Night Flower: Inside AIPAC 's Fight for Influence.'**

Watch the groundbreaking film above, which follows the powerful and polarizing
pro-Israel lobby from its roots as a one-man advocacy operation to the present
day, where it plays a key role in the U.S. elections. It features interviews
with multiple former AIPAC officials and insiders, members of Congress such as
Reps. Thomas Massie and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and leading activists as it
examines America's most influential pro-Israel lobbying group.

**" Always remember, a lobby is a night flower,"** former AIPAC staffer M.J.
Rosenberg recalls being told on his first day. "**It blossoms in the dark and
withers in the sun. "**
